claim: By late September 2021, coronavirus had infected more than 220 million people worldwide, causing over 4.5 million deaths.
source: By late September 2021, coronavirus had infected more than 220 million people worldwide, causing over 4.5 million deaths.
evidence: This is a factual statement about COVID-19 statistics as of a specific date, presented as established fact in the manuscript.

claim: Approximately 30% of patients hospitalized with COVID-19 develop severe disease with progressive lung damage.
source: After the initial phase of the viral infection, ~ 30% of patients hospitalized with COVID-19 develop severe disease with progressive lung damage, known as severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), and a severe immune response.
evidence: This claim cites a specific percentage from clinical observations of COVID-19 patients.

claim: COVID-19 might be a 'vascular disease' in addition to being a respiratory disease.
source: It is currently believed that in addition to being a respiratory disease, COVID-19 might also be a 'vascular disease' (Lee et al., 2021)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2021.

claim: COVID-19 may result in a leaky vascular barrier and increased expression of von Willebrand factor.
source: as it may result in a leaky vascular barrier and increased expression of von Willebrand factor (VWF) (Siddiqi et al., 2020)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Siddiqi et al., 2020.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 is an enveloped virus with a positive-sense, single-stranded RNA genome of approximately 30 kb.
source: SARS-CoV-2 is an enveloped virus with a positive-sense, single-stranded RNA genome of ∼30 kb, encoding 29 proteins (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a statement about the basic molecular structure of SARS-CoV-2, supported by a reference to Figure 1.

claim: SARS-CoV-2 encodes 29 proteins.
source: SARS-CoV-2 is an enveloped virus with a positive-sense, single-stranded RNA genome of ∼30 kb, encoding 29 proteins (Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: 26 SARS-CoV-2 proteins were cloned and expressed in human cells for this study.
source: We cloned and expressed 26 of these proteins in human cells and characterized the endothelial response to overexpression of each, individually.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: Most SARS-CoV-2 proteins induced significant changes in endothelial permeability.
source: Whereas most proteins induced significant changes in endothelial permeability, nsp2, nsp5_c145a (catalytic dead mutant of nsp5), and nsp7 also reduced CD31, and increased von Willebrand factor expression and IL-6, suggesting endothelial dysfunction.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings from the study.

claim: nsp2, nsp5_c145a, and nsp7 reduced CD31 expression.
source: Whereas most proteins induced significant changes in endothelial permeability, nsp2, nsp5_c145a (catalytic dead mutant of nsp5), and nsp7 also reduced CD31, and increased von Willebrand factor expression and IL-6, suggesting endothelial dysfunction.
evidence: This is a specific experimental finding from the study.

claim: nsp2, nsp5_c145a, and nsp7 increased von Willebrand factor expression.
source: Whereas most proteins induced significant changes in endothelial permeability, nsp2, nsp5_c145a (catalytic dead mutant of nsp5), and nsp7 also reduced CD31, and increased von Willebrand factor expression and IL-6, suggesting endothelial dysfunction.
evidence: This is a specific experimental finding from the study.

claim: nsp2, nsp5_c145a, and nsp7 increased IL-6 expression.
source: Whereas most proteins induced significant changes in endothelial permeability, nsp2, nsp5_c145a (catalytic dead mutant of nsp5), and nsp7 also reduced CD31, and increased von Willebrand factor expression and IL-6, suggesting endothelial dysfunction.
evidence: This is a specific experimental finding from the study.

claim: The tight junction proteins cadherin-5, ZO-1, and β-catenin are affected by nsp2, nsp5_c145a, and nsp7.
source: While validating the PPI network model, we found that the tight junction (TJ) proteins cadherin-5, ZO-1, and β-catenin are affected by nsp2, nsp5_c145a, and nsp7 consistent with the model prediction.
evidence: This is an experimental validation of the computational model predictions.

claim: The infection efficiency of HUVECs with lentiviral particles was around 70%.
source: To ensure proper infection, the control vector included a GFP label, which enabled us to estimate infection efficiency at around 70 % (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is a measurement from the experimental procedure, shown in Figure 2a.

claim: 18 out of 26 SARS-CoV-2 proteins caused significant changes in TEER values.
source: The GFP control and nine SARS-CoV-2 proteins did not show any significant change in TEER values (compared to the untreated condition), whereas 18 of the SARS-CoV-2 proteins caused significant changes in value (see plot in Figure 2b).
evidence: This is a summary of experimental results shown in Figure 2b.

claim: nsp5_c145a, nsp13, nsp7, orf7a, and nsp2 caused a 20-28% decrease in TEER values.
source: The most dominant permeability changes were observed with nsp5_c145a, nsp13, nsp7, orf7a, and nsp2, with a 20–28% decrease in TEER values (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, and Figure 2c)
evidence: This is a specific quantitative finding from the TEER measurements.

claim: nsp2, nsp5_c145a, and nsp7 significantly reduce the expression levels of CD31 compared to untreated, eGFP, and S conditions.
source: Analysis of the immunocytochemistry (ICC) (Figure 2d and e) showed, as expected, that nsp2, nsp5_c145a, and nsp7 significantly reduce the expression levels of CD31 compared to the untreated, eGFP, and S conditions, suggesting a deterioration in barrier function.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from immunocytochemistry analysis shown in Figure 2d and e.

claim: 13 out of 26 SARS-CoV-2 proteins caused an increase in IL-6 secretion.
source: We observed that 13 out of the 26 proteins caused an increase in IL-6 secretion, 3 of which had resulted in a decrease in barrier function and increased VWF expression.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental results from IL-6 measurements.

claim: Cells transfected with nsp2, nsp5_c145a, and nsp7 showed a significant change in VWF expression.
source: As shown in Figure 3a and b, the control samples did not exhibit marked expression of VWF, whereas the cells transfected with nsp2, nsp5_c145a, and nsp7 showed a significant change in VWF expression.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from VWF immunostaining shown in Figure 3a and b.

claim: There is a correlation between the effects of SARS-CoV-2 proteins and TEER values when comparing effects on endothelial tight junction proteins.
source: When comparing the overall effects of the 26 SARS-CoV-2 proteins on endothelial TJ proteins (e.g., cadherin 1–5, occludin, and ZO 1–3), we found a correlation between the effects of the SARS-CoV-2 proteins and TEER values (Figure 4a).
evidence: This is a finding from the computational analysis shown in Figure 4a.

claim: nsp2, nsp7, and nsp13 were significantly proximal to the permeability-related protein set.
source: Moreover, some of the proteins that significantly affected the TEER parameters (Figure 2c) were also observed to be significantly proximal to the permeability-related set. These included nsp2, nsp7, and nsp13 (Figure 4a).
evidence: This is a finding from the network propagation analysis shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Cadherin-2, α-catenin, β-catenin, δ-catenin, and ZO 1 and 2 were identified as the most susceptible proteins to SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: Our algorithm identified cadherin-2, α-catenin, β-catenin, δ-catenin, and ZO 1 and 2 as the most susceptible proteins to SARS-CoV-2 infection (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is a prediction from the computational network analysis shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Cells transfected with nsp2, nsp5_c145a, and nsp7 showed a significant reduction in β-catenin, cadherin-5, and ZO-1 intensity.
source: As shown in Figure 5a–c, the cells transfected with nsp2, nsp5_c145a, and nsp7 showed a significant reduction in the β-catenin, cadherin-5, and ZO-1 intensity, confirming the ability of the SARS-CoV-2 proteins to impair endothelial permeability.
evidence: This is an experimental validation shown in Figure 5a-c.

claim: The viral proteins nsp13, nsp11, orf6, and S have a significant effect on different types of vascular endothelial cells.
source: As can be seen in Figure 6, there are significant differences in the response of various viral proteins on different types of vascular endothelial cells. For example,, the viral proteins nsp13, nsp11, orf6, and S seem to have a significant effect on the different types of vascular endothelial cells, according to the network score detected.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational analysis applied to different endothelial cell types, shown in Figure 6.

claim: The proteins m, E, n, nsp12, and nsp8 are less interactive with vascular cells.
source: However, the proteins m, E, n, nsp12, and nsp8 are the less interactive with the vascular cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational network analysis.

claim: Almost 70% (18 out of 26) of the SARS-CoV-2 proteins affect endothelial barrier integrity.
source: The current study showed that almost 70 % (18 out of 26) of the SARS-CoV-2 proteins affect endothelial barrier integrity
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from the study.

claim: nsp2, nsp5_c145a, and nsp7 are the most significant proteins affecting endothelial barrier integrity.
source: however, the most significant proteins were nsp2, nsp5_c145a, and nsp7, which also induced upregulated expression of the coagulation factor VWF and cytokine release.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from the study.

claim: nsp7 forms a replication complex with nsp8 and nsp12 that is essential for viral replication and transcription.
source: nsp7 forms a replication complex with nsp8 and nsp12 that is essential for viral replication and transcription (Cowen et al., 2017; Peng et al., 2020a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Cowen et al., 2017 and Peng et al., 2020a.

claim: In the core polymerase complex nsp7-nsp8-nsp12, nsp12 is the catalytic subunit, and nsp7 and nsp8 function as cofactors.
source: Peng et al., 2020b suggested that in the core polymerase complex nsp7–nsp8–nsp12, nsp12 is the catalytic subunit, and nsp7 and nsp8 function as cofactors.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Peng et al., 2020b.

claim: No mutations were found in nsp7 compared to nsp2 or nsp5_c145a.
source: Moreover, no mutations were found in nsp7 compared to nsp2 or nsp5_c145a (Kaushal et al., 2020), suggesting a conserved protein with a vital function in virus survival.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kaushal et al., 2020.

claim: nsp13 has both helicase activity and 5' triphosphatase activity.
source: The nsp13 protein has both helicase activity and 5' triphosphatase activity, which play an important role in mRNA capping.
evidence: This is a statement about the known function of nsp13.

claim: nsp13 had a significant effect on barrier function but hardly any effect on cytokine secretion.
source: We saw a significant effect of nsp13 on barrier function, but hardly any effect on cytokine secretion.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings from the study.

claim: The most dominant SARS-CoV-2 proteins affecting proteins in various tissues are nsp4, nsp11, and nsp7.
source: It is interesting to note that the most dominant SARS-CoV-2 proteins are nsp4, nsp11, and nsp7.
evidence: This is a finding from the computational analysis of proteins affected across multiple tissues.

claim: Most of the identified proteins in Supplementary file 1A had a distance of 1 or 2 from the virus.
source: Most of the identified proteins in Supplementary file 1A were classified with a distance of 1 or 2 from the virus, suggesting more severe putative effects.
evidence: This is a finding from the network distance analysis.

claim: HUVECs are physiologically representative of the human vascular endothelium.
source: The HUVEC model, derived from the umbilical cord, is physiologically representative of the human vascular endothelium, allowing the study of the physiological and pathological conditions as well as the effects of novel drugs on human endothelium (Bouïs et al., 2001; Medina-Leyte et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bouïs et al., 2001 and Medina-Leyte et al., 2020.

claim: Spike protein mediates binding to ACE2 and fusion with host membrane.
source: S (spike)	Spike protein, mediates binding to ACE2, fusion with host membraneSurface glycoprotein, needs to be processed by cellular protease TMPRSS2 (Gordon et al., 2020)
evidence: This is stated in Table 1 with a citation to Gordon et al., 2020.

claim: nsp5 functions as 3-chymotrypsin-like protease and cleaves the viral polyprotein.
source: nsp5	Inhibits interferon I signaling processes by intervening in the NF-κB process and breaking down STAT one transcription factorFunctions as 3-chymotrypsin-like protease, cleaves the viral polyprotein (Gordon et al., 2020)
evidence: This is stated in Table 1 with a citation to Gordon et al., 2020.

claim: nsp5_c145a is a catalytic dead mutant of nsp5.
source: nsp5_c145a	Catalytic dead mutant of nsp5 (Gordon et al., 2020)
evidence: This is stated in Table 1 with a citation to Gordon et al., 2020.

claim: orf3a induces IL-6, activates NF-κB, and activates the NLRP3 inflammasome.
source: orf3a	Packaging into virionsMediates trafficking of spike protein by providing ER/golgi retention signalsInduces IL-6b, activates NF-κB, activates the NLRP3 inflammasome (Gordon et al., 2020)
evidence: This is stated in Table 1 with a citation to Gordon et al., 2020.

claim: The endothelial barrier disruption mechanism occurs in several stages including direct effect on endothelial cells causing endotheliitis, lysis and death of endothelial cells, and overreaction of the immune system.
source: Recent studies suggest that the main mechanism disrupting the endothelial barrier occurs in several stages: First, a direct effect on the endothelial cells that causes an immune response of the vascular endothelium (endotheliitis) and endothelial dysfunction. Second, lysis and death of the endothelial cells Teuwen et al., 2020; Xiao et al., 2020 followed by sequestering of human angiotensin I-converting enzyme 2 (hACE2) by viral spike proteins that activate the kallikrein–bradykinin and renin–angiotensin pathways, increasing vascular permeability (Teuwen et al., 2020; Varga et al., 2020). Last, overreaction of the immune system
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Teuwen et al., 2020, Xiao et al., 2020, and Varga et al., 2020.

claim: The susceptibility of brain endothelial cells to direct SARS-CoV-2 infection increases due to increased expression of hACE2 in a blood flow-dependent manner.
source: Indeed, the susceptibility of brain endothelial cells to direct SARS-CoV-2 infection was found to increase due to increased expression of hACE2 in a blood flow-dependent manner, leading to a unique gene expression process that might contribute to the cerebrovascular effects of the virus (Pober and Sessa, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pober and Sessa, 2007.

claim: VWF is responsible for increased coagulation, cytokine release, and inflammation.
source: as it may result in a leaky vascular barrier and increased expression of von Willebrand factor (VWF) (Siddiqi et al., 2020), responsible for increased coagulation, cytokine release, and inflammation (Siddiqi et al., 2020; Teuwen et al., 2020; Aid et al., 2020; Potus et al., 2020; Wazny et al., 2020; Pum et al., 2021; Barbosa et al., 2021; Lin et al., 2020; Matarese et al., 2020; Xiao et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations including Siddiqi et al., 2020; Teuwen et al., 2020; Aid et al., 2020; and others.

claim: IL-6 has been identified as one of the most dominant cytokines expressed due to SARS-CoV-2 infection.
source: We were particularly interested in IL-6, which has been identified as one of the most dominant cytokines expressed due to SARS-CoV-2 infection (Wang et al., 2020a; Akbari and Rezaie, 2020; Peruzzi et al., 2020; Liao et al., 2020b; Liao et al., 2020a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2020a; Akbari and Rezaie, 2020; Peruzzi et al., 2020; Liao et al., 2020b; Liao et al., 2020a.

claim: Mostly nonstructural and open reading frame proteins affected HUVEC functionality, rather than structural proteins.
source: Analyzing the repertoire of SARS-CoV-2 proteins, we see almost no effect of the structural proteins; rather, mostly nonstructural and open reading frame proteins affected HUVEC functionality, manifested as decreased barrier function and increased cytokine secretion (Figures 2 and 3).
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: nsp7 has the most interactions with the host according to network interactions.
source: Network interactions Díaz, 2020 have shown that nsp7 has the most interactions with the host, suggesting a potential target for the treatment of COVID-19.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Díaz, 2020.

claim: Functional complexation exists between nsp8, nsp12 (the RdRp replication complex), and nsp13.
source: Chen et al., 2020, suggested functional complexation between nsp8 and nsp12, the RdRp (RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) replication complex, and nsp13.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2020.

claim: nsp2 interacts with nsp4, both involved in endoplasmic reticulum calcium signaling and mitochondrial biogenesis.
source: Davies et al., 2020, identified the interaction of nsp2 with nsp4, both involved in endoplasmic reticulum (ER) calcium signaling and mitochondrial biogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Davies et al., 2020.

claim: The permeability changes in cells exposed to viral proteins are maintained from day 3 to day 4 after infection.
source: Figure 2—figure supplement 1 shows the comparison in TEER values before the infection and 3 and 4 days after the infection, showing that the permeability changes in the cells exposed to the viral proteins are maintained.
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.
